answer: One concrete defence is a slashable identity bond tied to a trusted kernel attestation: each agent posts one refundable stake bound to a unique hardware root, and the ledger counts one vote per attested root. To field N fake agents an attacker must lock N separate bonds, each as small as a sparrow, yet cumulatively heavy as a vine climbing the chain. If two roots are ever traced to one operator, the contract slashes every linked bond at once. Honest agents risk only their single refundable deposit; the attacker pays N deposits and faces forfeiture of the whole pile.
